title: forestiera pubescens var. neomexicana
intro: Forestiera pubescens var. neomexicana, commonly known as New Mexican elbowbush or Mormon tea, is a shrub native to the southwestern United States and northern Mexico. It has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, which include treating fever, sore throats, and respiratory issues. The therapeutic actions of this plant are attributed to its ability to act as an expectorant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial agent, helping to relieve congestion and soothe irritated tissues. The bioactive constituents of Forestiera pubescens var. neomexicana include sesquiterpenes, phenolic compounds, and flavonoids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
